text:
josh: Hey support — since yesterday our on-prem bastion->egress path intermittently fails when calling the Redwood Private API. We see 502s from our proxy and TLS handshake timeouts in the client. We briefly flipped the proxy from explicit -> transparent mode earlier today which changed failure rate. Can someone help triage?

maria: Thanks Josh. Can you confirm this is a Private/VPC deployment and share a minimal curl repro + any client logs or tcpdump you captured? Also need account/org id.

josh: Confirmed Private (vpc). Org: acme-corp. Quick curl I just tried (sanitized):

```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health
* Connected to corp-proxy.corp (10.10.10.5) port 3128 (#0)\n* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to api.redwood.internal:443
> CONNECT api.redwood.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.internal:443
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
* Received HTTP/1.1 502 from proxy
* TLS handshake timeout (after 30s)\ncurl: (35) SSL connect error
```

Logs show intermittent TLS handshake timeouts and a few successful calls.

anil: A couple quick suspects: 1) the corp proxy might be rewriting or stripping SNI when it forwards traffic (common with some transparent modes), 2) hairpin SNAT from the bastion/NAT pool could cause asymmetric routing and conntrack drops, and 3) some proxies downgrade CONNECT semantics (not tunneling) which breaks TLS routing on our edge. Do you have a tcpdump of the ClientHello reaching the proxy or the egress hop?

josh: I captured 1min of tcpdump. Observations: client initially sends ClientHello with SNI "api.redwood.internal". When the proxy uses explicit CONNECT+tunnel, the SNI reaches the remote host and call succeeds. When the proxy is in transparent mode or using an inline TLS-inspect appliance, I sometimes see the outgoing packet with SNI replaced to "internal-proxy" or the SNI absent entirely. Failures correlate with SNI missing/modified. Also noticed NAT port churn on the bastion — source port changes mid-flow in failing cases.

maria: That matches what we'd expect if the edge needs SNI to pick the correct cert/route. Our HTTP/2 and TLS1.3 path requires SNI for virtual hosting and cert selection. If SNI is stripped or rewritten, our frontend may select the wrong cert or drop the flow, producing 502s/backoff and apparent TLS timeouts. Two things to try immediately: 1) configure corp-proxy to tunnel CONNECT for api.redwood.internal (allow CONNECT to 443) or add a PAC rule to bypass proxy for that host (DIRECT), and 2) ensure NAT persistence on the bastion so source port doesn't change mid-session (increase SNAT table/timeouts, enlarge NAT pool).

anil: Agreed. For reproducible repro on your side run these variations and paste outputs:

1) explicit CONNECT via proxy (expected success):
```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate
```
2) bypass proxy to test no-inspect path (replace 34.111.22.33 with our example ELB IP you can resolve):
```
curl -v --connect-to api.redwood.internal:443:34.111.22.33 https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health
```
3) tcpdump filter: `tcpdump -i eth0 host <bastion-ip> and port 443 -w redwood-ssl.pcap` then check ClientHello SNI via tshark.

josh: Ran tests. CONNECT tunnel = success. Direct connect-to (bypass) = success. Transparent/proxy-inspect = fails with SNI replaced or absent. tcpdump + tshark confirm SNI present from client but replaced by appliance.

maria: Root cause summary: inline TLS inspection / transparent proxy was rewriting/stripping SNI and hairpin SNAT behaviour amplified intermittent failures (conntrack timeouts). Recommended remediation:
- Put api.redwood.internal on proxy bypass (PAC -> DIRECT) or configure proxy to use true CONNECT-tunneling for that host.
- If TLS inspection is required by policy, install the inspection CA into the bastion trust store (so client trusts proxied cert), but note this still rewrites SNI and may break our virtual host routing; tunneling is preferred.
- Increase NAT persistence / expand SNAT pool on the bastion to avoid source port churn.
- As a longer-term option, add a PAC rule targeting the bastion IP range to ensure egress flows for our Private endpoints are always tunneled.

josh: Implemented PAC bypass for api.redwood.internal and bumped NAT timeout — flows now stable. No TLS timeouts for ~90m :thumbsup: Thanks for the help.

maria: Awesome, glad that worked. We'll add a short runbook to our internal Private deployment docs for "on-prem bastion egress: proxy tunneling + NAT tips" and reference your ticket. If you want, we can also open a config check with our onboarding team to validate other customers' PACs.

support-bot: Ticket #12345 status updated -> resolved (customer confirmed). Runbook created: "egress-proxy-tunnel-sni-runbook"

josh: Thanks all, closing from my side.
